gap._description: Swift's modern surface is largely handled: actors/structs/enums/extensions (class_declaration + anonymous keyword token), protocols + associated types, operators, subscripts, optional binding, error handling, macros, conditional compilation, and per-symbol cyclomatic complexity. Remaining gaps are exotic macro/type forms the pinned grammar parses but the analyzer does not yet emit as symbols.

gaps.node_type: operator_declaration, custom_operator, precedence_group_declaration, precedence_group_attributes, precedence_group_attribute, deprecated_operator_declaration_body
gaps.missing: custom operator + precedence-group declarations as symbols (operator overloads on types ARE handled; file-scope operator/precedence declarations are not)
generic packs and fully-open ranges as distinct symbols

gaps.node_type: key_path_expression, key_path_string_expression, selector_expression, constructor_expression, constructor_suffix, metatype, opaque_type, existential_type

decisions.question: The pinned grammar (alex-pinkus style) has ONE class_declaration node for class/struct/actor/enum/extension — the kind is decided by the anonymous keyword token.
decisions.resolution: The analyzer reads the anonymous keyword token (class/struct/enum/extension/actor) to pick the kind — never source-text scanning. Only CLASS can have a superclass: its FIRST base is extends ONLY when that base is a class. A first-base protocol is still an adoption (implements). Kind resolution: an in-file pre-pass records declared protocol/class names, and the cross-file companion (context.typeKinds, corpus protocol set) covers other files; unknown externals follow the deterministic Swift rule (first base = superclass extends). Structs and actors have NO superclass — every base is implements.

decisions.question: Operator overloads (`static func + (l:r:)`) have no simple_identifier name — the name is the anonymous operator token after `func`.
decisions.resolution: Emitted as method symbols named `operator +` / `operator ==` / `operator []` (the dart #265 operator-signature convention); their bodies' calls/instantiates attach to the operator method.

decisions.question: Subscript READS (`entries[key]`) parse as call_expression with a `[key]` call_suffix — indistinguishable from a function call by node type alone.
decisions.resolution: A call_suffix whose value_arguments open with `[` is a property read — NO calls edge (family property-read precedent). `defer { }` also parses as a call_expression; it is filtered as a keyword construct, never a calls edge.

decisions.question: Swift inits have no distinct name; deinit and subscripts are not first-class symbols.
decisions.resolution: init -> constructor named "constructor" (Java/C# family convention); deinit and subscript are NOT symbols (ObjC dealloc / C# indexer precedent) but their bodies' calls still emit with the enclosing type as source.

decisions.question: `self.x` member READS vs `self.method()` CALLS both parse as navigation_expression.
decisions.resolution: A navigation_expression that is the callee of a call_expression is a CALL (calls edge to leaf); otherwise with a self receiver it is a member read (uses edge, source = enclosing type, target = leaf).

decisions.question: Is where_clause a real, fixture-coverable shape in the pinned grammar?
decisions.resolution: No. Probe-verified 2026-09-02: generic `where T: Equatable` clauses parse as type_constraints (with where_keyword + type_constraint children); no Swift source produces a where_clause node. The grammar declares it but it is unreachable. Reclassified from handled_verified per the F6 fixture-coverage gate (M14.0.F6).

decisions.question: The Pass-3 first-parent fallback emitted its GUESS at confidence 1.0 with evidenceClass 'structural' — indistinguishable from a verified override in thresholded analysis. What is the correct tier contract?
decisions.resolution: M37.10 ruling (family-wide): verified overrides (in-file Pass-1) stay @1.0/structural; the Pass-3 first-parent guess is @0.5 with reasonCode 'first-parent-guess' and tier 'inferred' (classifyEvidenceTier <0.9 branch) — matching java/groovy's documented Pass-3 contract and staying below the patterns.ts 0.7 threshold. The guess may target a parent that never declares the method; claiming structural hid the evidence gap. Gated by F9-PROBE-M3710-SWIFT, the swift/external-override fixture + confidence pins, and 6 family regression mutants.

decisions.question: Protocol inheritance (`protocol A: B, C`) emitted NO edge — a comment claimed ObjC `@protocol A <NSObject>` precedent, but the managed-OO family materializes interface extends (csharp `interface IX : IA` -> extends, java `interface IX extends IA` -> extends, objc `@protocol B <A>` -> extends). Probe-verified 2026-09 on swift-nio: 46 protocol-inheritance sites, both sides silent.
decisions.resolution: protocol inheritance now emits extends per parent (weight 1). AnyObject/Any inheritance_specifiers are CLASS-CONSTRAINT markers, not protocol parents — probe-verified (`protocol P: AnyObject, B` in swift-nio parses AnyObject as an inheritance_specifier) — excluded from the extends set.

decisions.question: Extension conformances (`extension Circle: Equatable`) emitted NOTHING — base extraction was skipped for the Extension kind. Swift forbids redundant conformances, so every extension base is an ADDITIONAL adoption. Corpus: 380 sites in swift-nio (554 files). csharp partial-class conformance is the managed-OO analog and IS materialized.
decisions.resolution: extension bases now emit implements (weight 0.9) sourced from the extension symbol (named after the extended type). Extensions cannot add a superclass, so no extends is ever possible.

decisions.question: Enum bases were skipped entirely AND the first base was always recorded as rawType metadata — so `enum Result: Error` minted bogus rawType=Error payload (Error is a conformance) and no conformance edges ever emitted. Corpus: 181 enums carry bases; ~93% first-slot are protocols (Sendable 76 / Error 46 / Hashable 22 / Equatable 17 / String 7 / Int 5 / UInt8 1).
decisions.resolution: only a stdlib-named first base (String/Character/Int8-64/UInt8-64/Float/Double/CGFloat) is the raw value (meta.rawType, no edge); every other base is a protocol conformance -> implements (weight 0.9). Mirrors dart DARTD15 (enhanced-enum conformances). Custom RawRepresentable raw types in first slot are unresolvable statically; the stdlib gate is the deterministic rule (accepted boundary).

decisions.question: Bare capitalized calls emit instantiates (Swift construction syntax), but two non-type families fabricate edges: XCTest assertion FUNCTIONS (XCTAssertEqual/XCTFail/... — the one capitalized free-function family in Swift; 8,226 of 13,966 capitalized bare calls = 59% in the swift-nio census) and stdlib fixed-width numerics (UInt64/Int64/UInt8 — 1,105 stdlib constructions — while Int/Double/String were already in BUILTIN_BARE_CALLS, an inconsistency). Both sides colluded (F5-blind).
decisions.resolution: XCT-prefixed bare callees are filtered (no edge — they are not types, matching BuiltinsAreFiltered); fixed-width stdlib numerics (UInt/UInt8-64/Int8-64) joined BUILTIN_BARE_CALLS. Genuine external type construction (DispatchQueue etc, undeclared in corpus) still emits instantiates. Oracle mirrored exactly.
